articles.title: How big swings in free agency built the Valkyries into a WNBA Finals team
articles.summary: Golden State's aggressiveness paid off.
articles.body:
In just their second WNBA season, the Golden State Valkyries are headed to the WNBA Finals and will open the championship series at home against the Atlanta Dream on Saturday.

Golden State can thank the rest of The W for its help in reaching the Finals after such a short period of time.

That's because the Valkyries have built a championship-caliber team by fielding a roster loaded with free-agent signings -- that is, players whose previous teams discarded them.

Take Kiah Stokes, for example. Stokes was the Las Vegas Aces ' defensive anchor on their 2022, 2023 and 2025 championship teams, but the Aces let her walk last spring and she joined the Valkyries on a two-year, $761,250 deal in April. Stokes played a significant role as the Valkyries swept the Aces out of the playoffs on Friday.

Gabby Williams arguably is the best player still standing in the playoffs . Williams signed a three-year contract in free agency with the Valkyries and has produced an All WNBA-caliber season, finishing behind Angel Reese in Defensive Player of the Year voting.

The Valkyries also convinced veteran reserve Tiffany Hayes to come out of retirement to search for her first championship, while the rest of the WNBA ignored French forward Janelle Salaun before Golden State signed her in 2025. Salaun won Sixth Player of the Year this season.

While Golden State drafted guard Kaitlyn Chen -- who has become another valuable reserve player -- much of the Valkyries' roster was put together via free agency and the expansion draft, where the franchise picked up Veronica Burton and Kayla Thornton, its first All-Star.

Top executive Ohemaa Nyanin deserves a ton of credit for identifying market inefficiencies, and head coach Natalie Nakase has forged a winning culture that has taken Golden State to the WNBA Finals.

With four more wins, the Valkyries' bold roster-building strategy will receive the ultimate validation: a championship banner inside Chase Center.

articles.title: Mensur Suljovic referred to darts regulator for inciting jeers against Ross Smith and alleged sexist comments as Austrian issues apology
articles.summary: Mensur Suljovic has been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority for his incitement of jeers against Ross Smith in their clash at the Swiss Darts Trophy; he has also been referred over his alleged sexist comments in an interview about the incident; the Austrian has issued an apology
articles.body:
The Austrian encouraged the crowd to boo the Englishman during a last-leg decider in their third-round clash at the Swiss Darts Trophy on Sunday afternoon.

He was later asked about the incident in an on-stage interview and used an allegedly sexist comment to describe how Smith reacted.

Suljovic said: "Ross Smith is one of the best players in the world - what's the bloke complaining about? He's got to play his game; otherwise, he's welcome to go home.

"Women, women - they're always complaining, sorry. Sorry, you don't do that. I fully accept him as one of the very best darts players.

"OK, I've been riling up the crowd a bit, just like in Germany - I need your support. I need you; without you, I can't achieve anything. Thank you, thank you very much!

"What's he complaining about? When I'm in England, everyone's against me; everywhere I go.

"And now, all of a sudden, he's complaining? He might as well just stay at home."

On Monday afternoon, Suljovic subsequently issued an apology.

"I would like to comment once again on my match against Ross Smith and the interview that followed," he said.

"The emotions got the better of me in that moment. I wanted to get the crowd behind me and, in doing so, I didn't properly realise that Ross was throwing for the match.

"Looking back, I understand that the timing was unfortunate and was perceived as unfair. I would like to apologise to Ross for that.

"Ross is, in my opinion, one of the best darts players in the world, and I have great respect for him and his achievements.

"My comment about women during the interview was also completely inappropriate. I should never have said something like that. I would like to sincerely apologise to all women for those remarks.

"Darts thrives on emotion, but fairness and respect are just as important. Yesterday, I let my emotions get the better of me.

In a statement, the PDC confirmed "the matter on stage and interview has now been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority" and issued "no further comment".

The incident between Suljovic and Smith explained

Suljovic and Smith were locked at 5-5 in their best-of-11-legs clash on Sunday afternoon, with Smith having two match darts at double 18 when Suljovic gestured to the crowd to increase the volume of boos, prompting the Englishman to miss the target and hand his opponent a chance to steal the match.

Suljovic then nailed double 10 with his final dart to complete the checkout and seal victory.

His antics had left Smith frustrated, with the Englishman later taking to X to share his thoughts following the defeat.

"I don't blame Mensur for me losing that game," Smith wrote. "I missed two match darts. Simple as that.

"Obviously, it's impossible for me to know what he's doing behind my back when I'm throwing apart from the crowd's response.

Suljovic is no stranger to controversial incidents. The Austrian denied intentionally provoking Joe Cullen during a World Championship clash last December.

Cullen branded his opponent's pace of play as "cheating" and "not darts" after becoming frustrated by the length of time he was taking to retrieve his darts and celebrate, with referee Kirk Bevans even forced to intervene.

Webster: There is a time and place for it and it was 'poor form'

Sky Sports Darts' Mark Webster on the incident between Smith and Suljovic (speaking before the apology)...

"Obviously with regards to the weekend, it was poor form for Mensur Suljovic.

"I think every player can use the crowd to their advantage, but there's a time to do it, isn't there?

"It's not while the player's throwing, particularly not on match darts.

"Fair play to Ross, he came out and said he didn't even see it and it didn't put him off, he still should have won the game.

"Mensur kind of doubled down on it as well. Like I said, get the crowd involved, players do it, it's part of the game now, but not on match darts and geeing them up when he's on match darts.

"He has used tactics in the past, hasn't he, in terms of slowing players down.

"That's fine, it's not against the rules, but sort of egging on the crowd when Ross on match darts wasn't good.

"I'm sure the DRA will get involved now, it's not good sportsmanship, is it? Rightly so, he should get fined.

"As long as he recognises that he's done wrong, he hasn't at the minute, but when he recognises that he's done wrong, it's the timing of it, isn't it, that's the poorest.

"I'm sure he'll realise and a fine will come his way. He should learn from it and he should never do it again, not on match darts."

articles.title: UK PM Andy Burnham met Man City chairman during time as Manchester mayor
articles.summary: Statement comes after criticism of Burnham’s initial response ⁠to City being found guilty of serious financial breaches.
articles.body:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham met Manchester City Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak at an investment summit several years ago when he was mayor of the city, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority has said.

The announcement on Monday comes after Burnham said he would be “really concerned” if City’s owners sold the football club following the decision to find the 10-time English champions guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules.

Burnham, who was mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to June 2026, faced criticism for appearing to express support for City’s hierarchy.

Downing Street subsequently had to backtrack, insisting no one was “above the rules”.

But there were demands for clarification regarding Burnham’s relationship with City’s owners, who have driven significant investment in Manchester through partnerships with local authorities.

City are owned by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), controlled by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a member of the United Arab Emirates’ royal family.

A Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) spokesman said: “In October 2021, Andy Burnham, in his role as mayor of Greater Manchester, had a formal meeting with Khaldoon Al Mubarak at the UK Government’s Global Investment Summit arranged by the Department for International Trade.

“In his capacity as mayor, he was a guest of Manchester City FC at home matches on a small number of occasions, including attending Vincent Kompany’s testimonial match in September 2019, where he met the chairman informally in the stands. These have been declared in the usual way.”

The statement added that during Burnham’s time as mayor “representatives of Greater Manchester sporting clubs would routinely join business delegations as part of mayoral international visits.

“This included representatives from Manchester United travelling to Austin and Dublin, Lancashire Cricket Club joining a delegation to India, and Manchester City FC staff supporting visits to China and Japan.”

But Louie French, the opposition Conservatives spokesman for sport, said the statement contained “precious little information about these meetings, what was discussed and what may have been agreed”.

It was far “from the full transparency that football fans deserve. Burnham cannot hide behind the GMCA – he must take responsibility for this himself”, French added.

City have been found guilty of breaking more than 100 Premier League financial regulations by arranging “sham” contracts to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs in a nine-season run between 2009 and 2018.

The Premier League leaders have appealed against the verdict, saying it contains “clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”.

City could be hit with a huge points deduction or even face expulsion from the Premier League if they lose the appeal.

articles.title: Yes, the SEC is still getting ridiculous preferential treatment in the AP Top 25 Poll
articles.summary: Texas dropped five spots after losing to unranked Oklahoma, while Alabama didn't budge after a home loss to Georgia in the latest AP Top 25 Poll.
articles.body: It's getting ridiculous. Well, it's past ridiculous. The SEC, somehow, keeps getting preferential treatment in the AP Top 25 Poll in a way no other conference does. For some reason. And this week's poll might be the best example yet of how the bias among poll voters continues to impact the college football season. Let's look at how the voters handled some of the biggest results of the weekend, compared to how they handled previous results from teams with the wrong patch on the front of their jersey. WEEK 6 AP TOP 25 POLL SEES A MAJOR MIXUP AND A NEW TOP TEAM IN THE COUNTRY AFTER AN UPSET-FILLED SATURDAY To start, we can look at the Texas-Oklahoma game. While the Longhorns outgained the Sooners both in total yardage and yards per play, they were set back by two terrible fourth quarter interceptions from quarterback Arch Manning. Both at the worst possible time. One was returned for a touchdown, and the other effectively allowed Oklahoma to win the game in regulation. The Sooners were not ranked entering the week, and for good reason. They lost on the road to Michigan, scored just 14 points against New Mexico, and were blown out by Georgia 41-13. They're not a very good team. Texas may have outplayed them, but the very clear flaws in Manning's game cost them the result. A neutral site game against a middling unranked team that scored 14 points at home against New Mexico. The punishment for the Longhorns? Dropping from No. 1 to No. 7. When Ohio State lost as the No. 1 team in the country, on the road to the then-No. 4 Longhorns by one point after a miraculous comeback, they dropped from No. 1 to No. 6. Similar punishments for wildly different "quality" losses. Then there's Alabama. The Crimson Tide lost, at home, to the Georgia Bulldogs in a close game, though the Bulldogs averaged a whopping 7.5 yards per play to just 5.8 for Alabama. Though the Tide were denied a clear and obvious pass interference penalty in the fourth quarter that may have changed the game. Still, it's a home loss. Yes, Georgia is good, and yes, the score was close, but poll voters typically punish any team for losing a home game. And remember, Ohio State lost on the road to the presumptive No. 1 team in the country and dropped five spots. Not Alabama! Remarkably, the Tide didn't budge, going from No. 6 to...No. 6. After losing. At home. Why even play the games when they don't matter? Ole Miss has received some exceptional SEC treatment too. The Rebels resume now looks worse and worse, thanks largely to Florida and LSU's poor play. The Gators went from the darlings of college football to deservedly unranked in just a few weeks after an embarrassing blowout loss at home to South Carolina. The same Florida team that dominated Ole Miss 52-28, scoring 35 points in the second half. LSU, meanwhile, lost on the road to an unranked Kentucky team, their second of the season. They entered the week at No. 9 in the AP Poll and after their resume took a huge hit, fell all the way to...No. 9. What about LSU? The Tigers spent a small fortune, at least $150 million, on hiring Lane Kiffin and revamping their roster. Thus far, they have an unimpressive 4-2 record to show for it, and with more tough games coming, an 8-4 finish might be the best case scenario. Two losses, no meaningful wins, and the Tigers somehow are still ranked No. 22. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Meanwhile, the Oregon Ducks have a win over a ranked team, No. 19 USC, and their two losses are to No. 18 Oklahoma State and No. 12 UCLA. Unranked. In fact, they're nearly 200 "points" behind the Tigers. Tennessee's big win this year is losing by three to Texas, yet they're ahead of other comparable one-loss teams. Why does this matter? Well, there's a clear and obvious advantage this list gives the SEC: ranked wins and ranked losses. Tennessee plays Alabama this week, a ridiculous No. 6-No. 14 game. What should be two teams in the No. 10 and No. 20 range now looks much more important. LSU inexplicably staying in the polls at No. 22 allows this weekend's contest against Mississippi State to be another "ranked" game. Meanwhile, Nebraska, who's 5-1 with one close home loss to Indiana, is playing Oregon while both are unranked. articles.title: Iowa State embraces ‘controllables’ as point guard shuffling continues
articles.summary: Cyclones look to second-year jumps and transfer playmakers to maintain physical edge amid backcourt injuries.
articles.body:
Iowa State head coach T.J. Otzelberger set an intense tone for the upcoming men's basketball season during media day Monday, emphasizing daily work habits, culture and relentless accountability as the Cyclones look to build upon last season's 29-win campaign.

Entering his sixth year leading the program, Otzelberger stressed that the Cyclones are embracing a daily grind focused on internal growth and development, establishing a foundation rooted in physical defense and competitive toughness regardless of roster fluidity.

The central storyline of the session revolved around senior guard Tamin Lipsey , who has returned to practice while awaiting clarification on his NCAA eligibility status.

Otzelberger confirmed that Lipsey is fully cleared medically and is steadily rebuilding his game conditioning after missing earlier live five-on-five scrimmages. Rather than dwelling on administrative uncertainty or legal proceedings, the coaching staff is actively preparing for two distinct operational blueprints—one with Lipsey directing the backcourt and one without him.

"I'm somebody that always looks at like what are the controllables and what are the things outside of your control," Otzelberger said. "And right now what's in the realm of our control is having Tamin in practice every day… Instead of speculate what that might look like, what we're going to do is be prepared. If Tamin's able to play, it's one scenario. If he's not able to play, it's another scenario."

Otzelberger emphasized that the program will focus strictly on variables within its control, refusing to spend time complaining about administrative delays or future eligibility rulings.

"There's not going to be any time we spend complaining, venting, expressing our frustration," Otzelberger said. "We're going to do the best job being the problem solvers we can with the situation and the task at hand."

That backcourt preparation has taken on added urgency with sophomore point guard Killyan Toure sidelined by an injury until at least January. To manage playmaking duties, Iowa State is relying on junior transfer Jaquan Johnson , a former Missouri Valley Conference standout who ranked among the national leaders in steals last season while posting a solid two-to-one assist-to-turnover ratio in practice. Redshirt senior transfer Ryan Prather Jr. , who previously led the nation in assist-to-turnover ratio, and freshman guard Yusef Gray Jr. are also taking on point guard responsibilities as the rotation adapts.

Up front, Iowa State expects major contributions from its returning core of second-year rotation players, tapping into a historical trend where Cyclones elevate their performance significantly in their second season. Otzelberger specifically highlighted player development coaches Nate Schmidt and Eric Crawford for driving that developmental leap, explaining that returners transition from learning the system's physical demands to becoming true program stewards.

"Something that's been consistent for us in our program is guys have made a big jump in year two," Otzelberger said. "The first year a lot of times guys come into a program there's a lot of learning and understanding and adapting, and then when you know what that is, now I feel like you're able to take a step from a performance standpoint, a leadership standpoint."

Senior forward Blake Buchanan anchors the defensive unit, earning the nickname "fireman" from Otzelberger for his elite ability to extinguish defensive breakdowns, switch onto perimeter guards, and protect the rim.

"For Blake, he brings so much to the table," Otzelberger said. "Defensively, his versatility, his ability to—call him a fireman on defense to put out fires and make plays—is elite."

Buchanan has also expanded his offensive repertoire with a refined short-range floater and improved free-throw shooting after contributing to last year's postseason run. Beside him, sophomore forward Dominykas Pleta has shown improved competitive stamina, with Otzelberger publicly encouraging Pleta to demand post touches and assert himself in the paint.

"Coach wants him to demand the ball," Otzelberger said. "We want to give him the ball more in the paint. We want the ball to hit his hands. We want him to seal and yell for the basketball. We know that he's a weapon. He's a force. He's bigger and stronger than he thinks he is."

Perimeter scoring will be heavily bolstered by sophomore guard Jamarion Batemon , whom Otzelberger envisions as a potential lead scorer and perimeter shooter. However, the coaching staff underscored that Batemon's offensive success remains directly tied to his defensive intensity, specifically his ball pressure and rebounding effort.

To maintain its trademark defensive identity, Iowa State added proven perimeter stoppers in Johnson and redshirt senior guard Leon Bond III . The frontcourt depth is rounded out by sophomore forward Tre Singleton —a Northwestern transfer who combines forward size with guard playmaking—redshirt senior forward Taj Manning , and athletic freshman forward Dorian Rinaldo-Komlan .

Freshman guard Christian Wiggins will miss the season following surgery , but drew high praise from Otzelberger for showing up to the gym immediately after his procedure to support his teammates.

"The day after surgery, he's the first guy in the building, the first guy in the gym," Otzelberger said. "Who knows what is even in his body, what meds and what's going on, but man, that was his way of saying, 'I'm with you guys. I may not be able to wear the uniform this year, but I'm with you."

Looking ahead to exhibition play against Creighton and the regular season, Otzelberger framed the year as a 150-day progression aimed directly at the Big 12 Conference Tournament in Kansas City.

"Individually and collectively we have 150 days until we play in the Big 12 conference tournament," Otzelberger said. "So if this group can embrace one day at a time for 150 days… you're going to be in a great spot when the dust clears and we end up going to Kansas City and playing at Hilton South."

Otzelberger emphasized that playing time and starting spots across the board will be strictly production-driven.

"It's going to be production driven and make your deal work," Otzelberger said. "The guys who are doing those things are going to get more and more opportunities on the day of the game… Once you get in the game, first time you get in the game, it's immediate impact."

articles.title: “May Go Down as the Curse of LeBron for Philadelphia”: Dave Portnoy Indirectly Blames LeBron James for Eagles’ Struggles
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are on a three-game losing streak. They have lost to the Chicago Bears, the Tennessee Titans and the Jacksonville Jaguars since Sept.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are on a three-game losing streak. They have lost to the Chicago Bears, the Tennessee Titans and the Jacksonville Jaguars since Sept. 29. The last loss to the Jaguars, falling 19-17 on Sunday, has put a real dent in their playoff hopes.

LeBron James signed with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. He had his first training camp practice with his new team on Sept. 29. Now, one would think there is no connection between James starting his 76ers career and the NFL team apart from being in the same city. However, Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy begs to differ.

Portnoy talked about the "LeBron curse":

"It may go down as the curse of LeBron for this Philadelphia city. And by the way, they'll (Philadelphia sports fans) be the first ones to say it. They don't like this guy."

"I was in Philadelphia doing pizza reviews, and I can't tell you how many Philly people came up to me and said, 'Curse word, LeBron.' They don't want him. There was a lot of talk about whether the curse of LeBron is now (hanging) over the city of Philadelphia. It is going to be a real conversation. … Since he's arrived, they haven't won anything. The Phillies got bounced from the playoffs, (Eagles offensive tackle) Lane Johnson retired, (Eagles coach Nick) Sirianni lost his brain; it's one bad thing (after another)," he said.

Cam Little becomes Jacksonville Jaguars' hero in 19-17 win

The Eagles had a strong first half. Jalen Hurts and Darius Cooper helped the Eagles to enter halftime with a 14-7 lead. However, things got worse for Nick Sirianni's team. Will Shipley, Michael Carter II, Jalyx Hunt and Tyler Steen all suffered injuries and were ruled out for the second half.

Cam Little led the fight back for the Jaguars. They ended the third quarter cutting the lead to 14-10 with his 34-yard field goal. There was some high-intensity drama awaiting with just eight seconds remaining on the clock. Ameer Abdullah ran for a 53-yard return to set Little up for a 57-yard game-winning field goal as time expired, handing the Eagles (2-3) their third straight loss.

It is clear that the squad's fitness levels are a shambles , while the lack of depth in certain positions is hurting Michael Carrick significantly.

The head coach had demanded INEOS sign a left-back as well as a backup striker, while it was also clear that defensive reinforcements were necessary.

Yet, the co-owners opted to focus only on the midfield and even then, they botched their operations.

With Carrick currently without a left-back and a specialist striker, the 20-time English league champions' hopes of steering the ship away from choppy waters seem to be fading.

"In the January window, United would consider signings if form stays poor and the right players become available.

articles.title: Former Man United duo of Jesse Lingard and Memphis Depay set for intriguing new chapter under Clarence Seedorf

articles.body:
Former Manchester United stars Jesse Lingard and Memphis Depay are set to join forces with legendary midfielder Clarence Seedorf at Corinthians.

Seedorf has returned to management as the new head coach of Brazilian side Corinthians.

It is Seedorf's first coaching role since 2019, when he was in charge of the Cameroon national team. The Dutchman has put pen to paper on a contract until the end of 2027.

He joins Corinthians while they are 16th in the Brazilian top flight, one place above the relegation zone with eight games left to play.

Seedorf takes over from former Brazil interim national coach Fernando Diniz, who was dismissed last week after Corinthians lost seven games in a row.

In addition to Cameroon, Seedorf has previously managed AC Milan, Shenzhen FC, and Deportivo La Coruña.

Seedorf said [as quoted by GOAL ], "Accepting this challenge is an honour, but also a great responsibility. I am here to give my all and build a team that fights for every ball, every minute, every victory."

He lands the role days after visiting United's Carrington training complex for a candid chat with Kobbie Mainoo .

Mainoo has drawn comparisons with Seedorf due to their similar playing style. The pair talked about Mainoo's dreams and ambitions. The United ace also opened up on the difficulties he faced during Ruben Amorim's spell in the dugout.

Seedorf will work with two former United players at Corinthians: Depay and Lingard.

Depay joined Corinthians in September 2024, having left Atlético Madrid as a free agent. He came close to departing the club during the summer amid a bitter dispute; however, he ultimately remained.

Meanwhile, Lingard signed for Corinthians in March this year, having been a free agent since parting ways with Korean side FC Seoul at the end of 2025.

Lingard was on the radar of MLS clubs but opted to move to Brazil.

articles.title: Why Kimi Antonelli was left fighting his Mercedes brakes during the Singapore GP
articles.summary: The Mercedes driver struggled with poor stopping power behind traffic
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli left the Marina Bay Circuit with another podium finish and a 102-point lead over team-mate George Russell . He is indeed in control of the drivers' championship with another great race under his belt. But he almost left the track after putting his Mercedes into a barrier because the brake pedal started misbehaving.

The third-place finish behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc hid a surprisingly fraught drive.

Antonelli's race started with an issue before the lights even turned off as the team found a brake sensor fault while the car was sat on the grid. The fix was carried out there and then, but the team had to run his car without any brake data.

More issues came during the race when the young Italian complained of having no stopping power. During the press conference following his Singapore campaign, he answered questions of how he drove around the issue.

"Well, just trying to lift and coast before every braking and to arrive a bit slower and put less pressure on the pedal," he said. "Because especially on the restart of the VSC, when I went to brake, nothing happened. I had really poor stopping, brake power and I almost went into the wall.

"So, it was just very tricky out there, and also the pedal was very long. But it was also kind of expected. You know, I've run three-quarters of the race behind a car in dirty air and obviously being so hot.

"Plus, we also had the sensor issue on the brakes, so we didn't even have the data about the brakes. We didn't know exactly what temperature they were running, so it was all about feeling. But they were hot because I could even smell it, so it was not very pleasant."

The new package still has a narrow operating window

The title leader was also asked about the upgrade package he ran on the Mercedes for the second time after the car failed to deliver in Malaysia.

"I think on this track, not yet," Antonelli admitted. "On this track, where you have a lot of slow speed, still not quite there in terms of performance. It's just because with the old package, you know exactly where to put the car, which window, and the car works very nicely.

"With this new package, we see the potential, the performance that it can bring, and I do feel it in certain corners. But the window is just too small of where the car operates at this moment. So also in driving, it's very sensitive to any differences that you do in the way you approach a corner or how you attack braking.

"So, I feel like, yes, the package is going to be faster and it's going to be, yeah, I think it can be a good step forward once we understand how to use the full potential."

Austin will be the Brackley outfit's next opportunity.

articles.title: “I’d Fire Him”: Analyst Has Harsh Words For Dan Quinn After “OT Mess” Vs. Giants
articles.summary: The Week 5 showdown between the Washington Commanders and the New York Giants ended in a surprising tie as neither team managed to secure the win in overtime...
articles.body:
The Week 5 showdown between the Washington Commanders and the New York Giants ended in a surprising tie as neither team managed to secure the win in overtime. Dan Quinn's squad has now fallen to 1-3-1 after that tie, while the Giants go to 3-1-1.

During The Colin Cowherd Podcast, host Colin Cowherd talked about the tie and that it only resulted in Dan Quinn getting into more trouble, saying that this was a "fireable moment." Fellow analyst John Middlekauff agreed, saying that he would have fired Quinn if it was up to him after what The Volume called an "OT Mess."

"I know he's a nice guy, but I'd fire him," Middlekauff said. "This isn't the end of the game, you could have kicked the field goal at 45 seconds. The game's over, everyone's touched the ball, this is overtime, leave! Everyone was stagnant on this… Dan Quinn would have had to say something. Any coach from the history of the league would have taken over from the sideline and started screaming at Jayden Daniels."

Middlekauff noted that the Commanders had the ball in their hands in the closing seconds. He stated that the team could have kicked a field goal with 45 seconds remaining and won that game. He added that Dan Quinn could have also taken over and directed his players to do the right actions to win and not end up with a tie.

Dan Quinn Says Tie Was "My Responsibility"

During the post-game press conference, Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn had to face the press after his team failed to score in the closing seconds against the Giants, leading to the tie. The coach owned up , stating that it was his responsibility.

"The last sequence, we throw it out of bounds, we clock it, you give yourself a chance to kick it," he told reporters. "And we pride ourselves on those moments at the end of the game. And after the first-down run, still trying to gain more for the kick. The right call is honestly like, we can go clock it early and don't put ourselves in that spot, and that is my responsibility. Nobody else's. I'm gutted for our team. We were given a lot of ops [opportunities] tonight to go find our win in all three phases, and we did not seize them."

He also admitted that it was not quarterback Jayden Daniels' fault, as they could have finished it early with a kick and that they did not need to gain any more yards in order to make that field goal attempt possible.

articles.title: Vikings Receive Important Jordan Addison Injury News During Bye Week
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have received an important update on Jordan Addison's injury status during their bye week. The post Vikings Receive Important Jordan Ad...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings pushed their record to 5-0 in Week 5 with a 23-13 victory over the New Orleans Saints, and while their defense remains the star of the show for the Vikings, their offense is also showing signs of life. Making that development even more encouraging is the fact that this unit is nowhere near full health early in the year.

While Minnesota got Justin Jefferson back for this game, fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison missed the team's win over the Saints due to a hamstring injury. Seeing Addison not be able to suit up for this contest was understandably concerning, but with the Vikings on their bye week, it sounds like he shouldn't have to miss much time.

Vikings Set to Get Jordan Addison Back From Injury After Bye Week

Much has been made about Minnesota's offense, which features a new starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, this season. The problem is that this unit has virtually never been at full strength through five games, with Murray and Jefferson both missing time and only recently sharing the field with each other.

Add in Jordan Mason, who is on injured reserve, and injuries that Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Aaron Jones are all dealing with, and it's safe to say the team's bye week has come at a good time. Through four games, Addison has caught 11 passes for 163 yards and a touchdown, and while those aren't huge numbers, he's helped hold things together on offense early on this year.

Addison was always viewed as unlikely to play in Week 5, and sure enough, he ended up being inactive for the game. Despite that, Addison participated in a pregame workout on Sunday, and according to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, the general consensus is that he should be able to return to the field for the Vikings' next game in Week 7.

"He is out with a hamstring injury. Worked out pregame last week, didn't have a great chance to go, but worked out pregame. That is a sign he is expected back," Rapoport said on "The Aftermath."

Vikings Aiming to Get Healthy During Their Bye Week

The fact that the Vikings have won each of their first five games, despite operating at less than peak efficiency on offense, is pretty encouraging. If everyone can get healthy, and Murray can continue to pick up the offense, Minnesota could very well wind up becoming the best team in the league.

For now, the team's main focus will involve enjoying some much-needed downtime and getting its key pieces like Addison healthy. When the Vikings return to action in Week 7, they will have an important contest against the Indianapolis Colts on their hands as they look to keep their undefeated streak going and push their record to 6-0.

articles.title: Aces won't say why mascot dumped popcorn on Valkyries star's family
articles.summary: Video of the popcorn dustup went viral over the weekend.
articles.body:
The sister of Golden State Valkyries star Gabby Williams took to social media after Friday night's win to allege the Las Vegas Aces knew their mascot's popcorn stunt was happening in the family and friends section.

During Game 3 on Friday night, the Aces' jackrabbit mascot Bucket$ went into the stands during a timeout and dumped popcorn on a section of Valkyries fans. According to a post on X , the Aces called this the "unlucky row" of the game. A video on TikTok didn't catch the actual moment the popcorn was dumped on fans but did show the aftermath. Bucket$ is seen swinging the emptied bag of popcorn over his head with a spotlight on him, celebrating the prank. The video concludes with a Valkyries fan who had popcorn dumped on them arguing with a person in a white suit.

That person was Kayla Williams, the older sister of Golden State star Gabby. Kayla Williams played collegiately at the University of Nevada at Reno, with Gabby citing her sister as her own inspiration to play basketball. Kayla Williams attended Friday night's game with her daughter and, in a reply to the video when it was shared on X on Saturday, had multiple concerns about the Aces' stunt.

"My daughter has a corn allergy and her scalp and eyes immediately started burning and itching. So honestly it was beyond throwing popcorn," Kayla Williams wrote on X . She added the section "has been the visiting team family and friends section since 2018. To say they didn't know what they were doing is a choice."

The Aces did not respond to SFGATE's multiple requests for comment on Monday.

Kayla Williams referenced the incident with a quip shortly after the Valkyries beat the Aces to finish off a series sweep: "Now that we showed yall how to sweep, come sweep up the popcorn you dumped on the GSV family section." She also directly addressed why she was so upset at the end of the video.

"I appreciate yall. We're good. Our other family n friends in that row are good. We're in the finals. This was unfortunate truly," Williams wrote on Saturday. "But GSV is in the finals as a second year team. I needed to make sure people knew this wasn't just me crashing out as much as that girl made it look."

Using popcorn for an in-arena gag is not uncommon in basketball circles - for example, Chicago Bulls mascot Benny the Bull throws popcorn frequently. It's why some on social media thought Williams had to know this was a possibility. But in response to another fan , she said she has attended her sister's games in these seats ever since the Aces moved to Las Vegas in 2018 and, on the popcorn stunt in particular, had "NEVER EVER seen this happen."

articles.title: Matt Campbell Hot Seat: Top 5 Candidates Who Can Replace Penn State HC If Nittany Lions Make Mid-Season Decision Ft. Luke Huard
articles.summary: Matt Campbell’s Nittany Lions were dealt another harsh blow in the wake of the team’s 31-23 loss to USC on Saturday. The loss has Penn State on a three-game...
articles.body:
Matt Campbell's Nittany Lions were dealt another harsh blow in the wake of the team's 31-23 loss to USC on Saturday. The loss has Penn State on a three-game losing streak, seemingly putting the team's chances of making a run in the playoffs on life support. The Nittany Lions are a proud organization with a recent history of success, so patience might be wearing thin.

If Campbell is given his walking papers before the end of the season, the team would need to figure out a successor in short order. Here's a look at some names that could be on the table to kick-start the next era.

5 Most Likely Replacements for Matt Campbell if Nittany Lions Move On

Lane Kiffin didn't wait until after the season to switch teams last year, so one's status as an employed coach does not exclude them from being a candidate. Brent Venables' Oklahoma Sooners have been underwhelming after falling out of the top 25 earlier this season.

If Venables feels the walls closing in, he might need to find a pivot before he suffers a public removal. The Nittany Lions could be one possible option to avoid that scene. If he is removed this year, he could still find himself as a top candidate for Penn State. Overall, Venables could give the Nittany Lions the ability to build something new and give himself a fresh start with two winning seasons in the last four years.

The Nittany Lions came up short to the USC Trojans on Saturday, and teams often choose to pluck pieces from teams that beat them. Lincoln Riley is surely off the table, but his offensive coordinator Luke Huard could be hungry for a promotion. According to Trojans media, Huard mentored quarterback Jayden Maiava to a nation-leading 91.2 QBR.

Quarterbacks are foundational to any football team, so a quarterback whisperer could be a great option for Penn State.

Dan Lanning's future with the Oregon Ducks is far from secure, with fans routinely calling for his job. At some point, the Ducks might bend under the pressure. If Lanning is removed before the end of the season, he might want to get as far from Oregon as possible. Penn State's location on the other side of the country could be a logical choice.

Lanning's run of four straight seasons with double-digit wins would give the Nittany Lions plenty of reason to consider him a top outside candidate.

While big names and up-and-coming outsiders could be one route the team could take, the Nittany Lions could keep the hire internal. Special teams coordinator Justin Lustig has already spent time with offense and defense via his work on special teams. As such, plenty of players know and respect him.

Lustig would logically be cheaper than trying to lure in a top candidate. Regardless of whether an outsider eventually gets the long-term goal in 2027, Lustig is a top candidate to take over immediately as an interim candidate if Matt Campbell is let go before the end of the season.

Taylor Mouser has experience working with star quarterback Brock Purdy (Penn State media), so he knows what works in the position. Under Mouser, Penn State's offense has hovered between explosive and competitive in every game this season. Twice, the Nittany Lions scored 45+ points. They lost only one game by multiple scores. As such, with the offense seemingly in better shape than the defense, giving Mouser the reins makes sense.

As an internal hire, he could be the team's interim coach if Matt Campbell exits early, which would give him the first shot at the job. Mouser wouldn't have to move, and he is more likely to ask for less than a premium hire.

articles.title: Colin Cowherd urges Broncos to plan for Bo Nix replacement
articles.summary: Colin Cowherd doesn't believe in Bo Nix.
articles.body:
Sports media personality Colin Cowherd is raising a question that would have seemed unthinkable just a few months ago: Should the Denver Broncos already be preparing for life after Bo Nix?

"You can't extend Bo Nix. You let the season play out… His first quarter passer rating is lower than Cam Ward and everybody thinks Cam Ward is a bust."@colincowherd thinks the Broncos need to start planning for Nix's replacement — Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) October 12, 2026

"You can't extend Bo Nix. You let the season play out… His first quarter passer rating is lower than Cam Ward and everybody thinks Cam Ward is a bust."@colincowherd thinks the Broncos need to start planning for Nix's replacement

Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) October 12, 2026

Following another uneven performance from Nix in Denver's 23-17 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 5 of the NFL season, Cowherd argued that the Broncos should let the season play out before making any long-term commitment to their quarterback.

Cowherd questions whether Nix is Denver's long-term answer

Oct 11, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) throws a pass against the Los Angeles Chargers during the first half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Cowherd did not suggest Denver should bench Nix immediately. Instead, he argued that the Broncos shouldn't rush into an extension before seeing how the rest of the season unfolds.

"You can't extend Bo Nix. You let the season play out," Cowherd said Monday. He then pointed to Nix's first-quarter passer rating, arguing it is lower than Cam Ward's—a quarterback many observers have already labeled a potential bust.

The criticism comes despite Denver sitting at 3-2 following Sunday's comeback victory over the Chargers. Nix completed 18 of 30 passes for 123 yards and a touchdown in the win, while Denver's defense did much of the heavy lifting in the fourth-quarter comeback.

Nix's overall 2026 numbers have been underwhelming compared with what Denver expected coming off his impressive 2025 campaign. Through five games, Nix has completed 97 of 162 passes for 942 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions. His passer rating is 80.8.

That is a significant decline from last season, when Nix threw for 3,931 yards, 25 touchdowns and 11 interceptions while leading Denver to the AFC Championship Game.

Broncos have bigger quarterback questions than their record suggests

Sep 14, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton prior to a game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The most concerning part for Denver is that Nix's struggles have coincided with an offense that has repeatedly struggled to generate consistency.

Sean Payton reclaimed play-calling duties entering Sunday's game after Davis Webb had handled them earlier in the season. The change was supposed to help create more rhythm, but Denver still produced only 224 total yards against Los Angeles.

Nix's first-quarter passer rating is 78.8 through five games, compared with a 90.8 rating in the second half. That disparity illustrates one of the biggest issues facing Denver: the Broncos have not consistently gotten enough from their quarterback early in games.

Cowherd's argument is therefore less about declaring Nix a bust and more about refusing to assume that last year's success automatically guarantees his future.

Denver has time to figure it out. The Broncos are winning games largely because their defense continues to give them opportunities, and Nix still has a substantial body of work from his first two seasons that cannot simply be ignored.

But if the offensive struggles continue, the Broncos will have a difficult decision to make. Rather than immediately handing Nix a massive extension, Cowherd believes Denver should keep every option open — including beginning to plan for a potential replacement.

articles.title: Middletown quarterback files injunction vs. OHSAA to remain eligible
articles.summary: The OHSAA ruled Middletown senior Kolby Morgerson ineligible under transfer bylaws after playing the first five games. His hearing is set for Friday.
articles.body:
A hearing involving the athletic eligibility of Middletown senior quarterback Kolby Morgerson will take place this week.

Morgerson's family has filed for a preliminary injunction against the Ohio High School Athletic Association to allow Morgerson to continue playing this season after he was ruled ineligible under transfer bylaws.

A hearing is scheduled for 9 a.m. Friday, Oct. 16, in the Butler County Court of Common Pleas.

Morgerson was the Middies' starting quarterback for the first five games of this season. He enrolled at Middletown in March after spending his first three seasons at Carlisle High School in Carlisle, Ohio, which is adjacent to Middletown to the north.

Under OHSAA bylaws, transfer students who play football are only permitted to play the first five games unless they meet one of the allowable exceptions that permit them to play the entire season, including playoffs.

Morgerson's family filed for an exception with the OHSAA, claiming they made a bona fide change of address, which the association denied. According to court documents, his mother, Bailey, took Kolby from Carlisle to a smaller residence in Franklin, in Middletown's district, because of a job change that caused financial hardship.

The Middletown City School District investigated the residence in Franklin. According to the court documents, the administration saw evidence that cast doubt on it being a permanent move. The OHSAA also shared text messages and social media posts by Bailey Morgerson, which they viewed as evidence the transfer was "athletically motivated."

In the filings, the school district said it would abide by whatever rulings the OHSAA and the court agreed upon.

The Morgersons' attorney, Bradley Kraemer, did not return requests for comment.

At Carlisle, Morgerson threw for over 4,300 yards and 39 touchdowns over the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Carlisle was 10-3 in 2025 with two playoff wins, with Morgerson throwing for 2,352 yards and 24 TDs.

Middletown reached the Division I state semifinals for the first time last season, and is 5-3 this year. Morgerson threw for 659 yards and five touchdowns in his five starts.

Morgerson has not committed to a college but according to his social media, he went to Ohio University for a recruiting visit Oct. 10.

This is one of multiple court battles between high school football players and the OHSAA this fall. Elder senior wide receiver Andrew Lyman reached a settlement agreement with the OHSAA last week, which allowed him to play additional games after initially being ruled ineligible after five games due to transfer restrictions.

articles.title: “Absolutely Disgusted”: Insider Makes Thoughts Clear on JMU’s Surprise Conference Realignment Move Amid Undefeated Season
articles.summary: After a 6-0 start to their season, the James Madison Dukes surprised many after announcing they will leave the Sun Belt Conference for the American Athletic...
articles.body:
After a 6-0 start to their season, the James Madison Dukes surprised many after announcing they will leave the Sun Belt Conference for the American Athletic Conference. The school announced that this will happen "no later than July 1, 2028," which means that for now, it is still with the SBC.

The announcement raised a lot of eyebrows, with CBS Sports' Bud Elliott calling out the school for choosing to leave the SBC for the AAC and saying these sorts of maneuvers are ruining college football.

"I am absolutely DISGUSTED that James Madison would abandon the Sun Belt for the American. What about loyalty? Tradition? The sanctity of conference membership? College football is being RUINED by schools selfishly pursuing their own interests," he posted on X.

JMU has been part of the SBC since 2022 as the school transitioned from the FCS to the FBS. The program gained prominence since then, as the likes of Curt Cignetti and Bob Chesney led the Dukes to much success. Now under Billy Napier, the Dukes are still undefeated this season.

When its AAC membership does become official, JMU will join other "full" members such as Alabama-Birmingham, Charlotte, East Carolina, Florida Atlantic, Memphis, North Texas, Rice, South Florida, Temple, Texas-San Antonio, Tulane, Tulsa and Wichita State, though Wichita State does not sponsor a football program. Army and Navy are also part of the AAC, but only in football.

JMU President Releases Statement on Leaving the SBC For the AAC

The official JMU Sports website was the one that revealed the school's planned move to the AAC. This included a statement from JMU President James Schmidt, saying that it was an honor to be accepted by the conference.

"We are honored that our request for membership in the American Conference has been accepted. I am grateful to Commissioner Tim Pernetti and the conferences' presidents and chancellors for their confidence in James Madison University," he said. "The American is home to member institutions who share our ambitious academic goals and our unwavering commitment to student success. Our student-athletes will compete in cities where JMU alumni are already rooted, and future Dukes will fill the stands. With this move, we carry deep appreciation for the Sun Belt Conference and its member institutions. Their partnership helped position JMU for this moment, and we are proud of everything we built together."

While JMU mostly competes in the Sun Belt, its lacrosse team has been competing in the American since 2022, winning two titles as an affiliate member. The school's swimming and diving teams have also begun competing in the AAC in the 2025-2026 season, with this latest move now solidifying that the school is fully moving to the American from the SBC.

articles.title: There's plenty of blame to go around for the Commanders' overtime-ending debacle vs. the Giants
articles.summary: No one involved is blameless for the Washington Commanders' game-ending debacle against the New York Giants in overtime.Coach Dan Quinn on Monday expressed f...
articles.body:
No one involved is blameless for the Washington Commanders' game-ending debacle against the New York Giants in overtime.

Coach Dan Quinn on Monday expressed frustration with multiple facets of the final play of the 27-27 tie , when Washington allowed the clock to run out while it was in range for a game-winning field goal.

With 55 seconds left and the ball at the Giants 26-yard line, the Commanders called a run play for Rachaad White that gained 2 yards and kept the clock moving. They substituted in multiple players and took their time snapping the ball, which didn't happen until 13 seconds left. A pass play was called, and Jayden Daniels took off running and was tackled inbounds without enough time left to run another play.

"Honestly just furious about our execution in the crucial moments of the game," Quinn said on a video call with reporters. "We worked really hard on these and it didn't look like yesterday."

Quinn said the team wanted to use more clock after getting into field goal range, considering there had been missed kicks from both teams — New York rookie Dominic Zvada was 2 of 5 on field-goal attempts, while Washington's Drew Stevens had already missed an extra point.

"It took entirely too long from there on to execute our strategy, from subbing to clock awareness to clocking the ball," Quinn said. "And what I told the team and the coaches is it was a breakdown that can't happen."

When asked about first-year offensive coordinator David Blough's role in the end-of-game scenario, Quinn took responsibility.

"It needs to be communicated then from me to David, who has the last words with Jayden on each down, not just a start of a drive," Quinn said. "And so when there's that time, you want to get to where the next one we're able to clock and kick. And so those are the ones in subbing and too slow with that, our execution was just off."

The play call itself was not unorthodox or unusual, Quinn said. But if the play had been run more quickly, the team would have had time to get back to the line of scrimmage, spike the ball to stop the clock and attempt a field goal.

Quinn agreed that the Commanders didn't show enough urgency, and that communication starts with him and has to flow from there. That begins with the substitutions, which Quinn said were unnecessary in hindsight.

Daniels' rushing ability. Playing with a brace on his left, non-throwing elbow after he dislocated it in Week 2, Daniels was effective as a rusher against the Giants. He finished with 103 yards rushing, including touchdowns of 38 and 26 yards.

Situational awareness. The Commanders had several miscues in the final minute of OT, one of which was Daniels' failure to recognize the situation and throw the ball away. Instead, he went down in the middle of the field.

"We have to stop the clock," Daniels said afterward. "We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me."

Chig Okonko. After missing two games (against the Cowboys in Week 2 and the Seahawks in Week 3), the tight end had four catches for 60 yards on six targets against the Giants. He had totaled four catches for 21 yards in his other two games this season.

Washington's second-half defense. The meltdown in the final minute obscured the fact that the Commanders allowed 24 points to the Giants in the third and fourth quarters.

New York scored three touchdowns and kicked a field goal on its final four possessions of regulation. In overtime, the Giants missed a field goal and fumbled in Commanders territory.

Excluding when Jameis Winston took a knee to end regulation, the Commanders allowed 332 yards on 56 plays — an average a 5.9 yards per play.

Quinn said that based on medical reports, he expects receiver Stefon Diggs (hamstring) and safety Nick Cross (illness) to return soon. Linebacker Javonte Jean-Baptiste suffered a pectoral injury, and Quinn said the team is awaiting more information.

95 — Second-half points allowed by the Commanders through five games. That includes 24 by the Giants.

The Commanders visit unbeaten San Francisco in a Monday night game on Oct. 19. Although the NFC East is considered wide open, Washington is two games behind the division-leading Giants and needs to stack wins in order to stay in the playoff mix.

articles.title: Why Lane Kiffin’s LSU is cooked after brutal loss to Kentucky
articles.summary: The Lane Kiffin era of LSU football is enduring rough turbulence. Kentucky created Kiffin and the Tigers’ biggest shakeup of 2026 on Saturday. LSU now entere...
articles.body:
The Lane Kiffin era of LSU football is enduring rough turbulence. Kentucky created Kiffin and the Tigers' biggest shakeup of 2026 on Saturday. LSU now entered Monday ranked No. 22, but falling 12 spots thanks to the 34-33 upset loss.

Yes, the Tigers aren't mathematically out of the conference championship race. The College Football Playoffs aren't out just yet either.

But a lot of external factors must come into play. And in diving deeper, here are the reasons why Kiffin's first season lands on the cooked side.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

LSU, Lane Kiffin haven't won big games together yet

The Ole Miss showdown handed Kiffin the ultimate chance of proving he was right to leave the playoff-bound Rebels for LSU. Plus prove he took over a more talented bunch compared to the place he left behind.

Except Ole Miss leaned into emotions and the star play of quarterback Trinidad Chambliss to prove Kiffin wrong. Although that loss kept LSU within the top 10 of the national rankings.

But the road trip to Lexington emerged as a massive deal for the SEC . Especially for a Wildcats team aiming to deliver their own noise in the loaded conference. That Saturday showdown presented UK coach Will Stein a chance to ignite national conversations about his team.

Kentucky clearly took the game more seriously compared to Kiffin's Tigers in the end. Kiffin saw a team that lacked execution and UK took advantage, delivering the statement overtime victory.

Kiffin lands at 0-2 against currently ranked top 25 teams this season. Proving that this LSU group still must learn to topple some of the nation's best if they want to establish themselves as a national title contender.

The road gets tougher from here for Lane Kiffin, LSU

So now Ole Miss and Kentucky sent the blueprint on how to beat Kiffin's Tigers. But that aforementioned winless mark could become worse for LSU.

Because the road to both the SEC title game and a spot in the 12-team postseason gets harder from here.

No. 16 Mississippi State is next on deck and the Bulldogs bring their own dynamic dual-threat in Kamario Taylor, despite his injury. LSU already struggled with Chambliss and UK's Kenny Minchey.

And the Bulldogs aren't even the highest ranked team LSU has left. No. 6 Alabama still comes to Baton Rouge and will be fueled by its loss to No. 1 Georgia. Then No. 7 Texas arrives the following week on Nov. 14. Finally, LSU has its pre-Thanksgiving road trip against No. 14 Tennessee.

That's four ranked teams still left on the Tigers' schedule. Granted, three of which head to Death Valley in Louisiana. But still, LSU already struggled with a previous top 10 ranked opponent in Ole Miss. And the likes of Mississippi State, Alabama and Texas have its own SEC title/CFP aspirations plus are led by coaches who have been at their posts longer. So LSU either catapults back into the national conversation or face a 6-6 finish in year one of Kiffin.

Signs already point to Kiffin and LSU simply needing to settle for a lesser bowl game and avoid the 5-7 finish at this point.

articles.title: Texas women's basketball player Jada Bediako out with Achilles tear
articles.summary: Before the season begins, Texas women's basketball player Jada Bediako tears her Achilles.
articles.body:
Head coach Vic Schaefer and Texas women's basketball will be down a Longhorn before the season even starts.

Jada Bediako , a senior transfer forward from Marquette, will miss with an Achilles injury.

An MRI confirmed the tear Monday and she will have surgery Thursday, Schaefer told reporters.

Due to the NCAA's new 5-for-5 rule , Bediako can return for a fifth and final season.

Her length at 6-foot-3 and experience was expected to make a great complement for junior forward Breya Cunningham . Bediako appeared in 26 games her junior year with the Golden Eagles. She shot 29 of 52 from the field and her 55.8% mark led the team in field-goal percentage.

After exhibition games against UConn and UCLA, Texas opens its season Nov. 4 against Fairleigh Dickinson at Moody Center.
